questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was very important for me to experience a completely different healthcare system and also how the relationship between the patient and doctor is in another country than Denmark. The japanese society is characterized by its conservative roots and since this is a very big difference between Denmark and Japan it is very intersting to see what kind of role it plays ind the relationship between the patient and the doctor. There is no doubt that there is many difference between these to countries which is why Japan is an ideal choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Some members of the administrative department helped me and gave me a lot of information. It was easy to always ask them if I had any questions and if they didn't have the answer they always got back to me.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above, some members from the administrative department welcomed me when I arrived. They showed me around campus, helped me to my dormitory and helped to go to the city hall to complete some documents in order to make me citizen of Isehara which apparently was necessary.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: As far as I am concerned it is possible to live at two different dormitories. I stayed at the Tokai University Isehara Staff Dormitory. I really appreciated this opportunity since it was affordable and near the hospital, so I could walk every morning to the hospital.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In the dormitory you had your own small kitchen and it was possible to cook small and easy meals. Otherwise it was possible to buy dishes at the supermarked which was already prepared and then you could just heat it in the kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It its affordable, you can walk to the hospital in about 20 minutes however it is quite far from the station and the supermarkeds in the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Because of the distance to the station from the dormitory it would have been nice to have a bicycle since the bus to the station from the dormitory doesn't operate too often.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied for the exchange program through my own university, UCPH and then I was accepted as their candidate. A few months later I received an email from the host university with some documents that I needed to fill out in order to register as a student at their university. I received my letter of acceptance rather late - 3 months prior to my exchange program was suppose to begin. I could contact the members of administration at the host university in order to get some help with filling out the documents they asked me to.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could contact the members of the administrative department at Tokai University and could help me if I had some questions. Otherwise it was more or less a feeling of I should just "trust the process".

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Since I study medicine I can only apply for a clinical clerkship at a host university that my own university corporate with. This means I don't have any choice to apply for different classes. But I was succesful with being accepted into the program I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: That you have to be patient. The process takes a long time. It is not difficult, but the different steps in the process takes quite a long time. So again you just have to trust the process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Again I was attending a clinical clerkship at a hospital and not specific classes so I don't really know about the level of the courses or classes. But I would say that from what I experience in my clinical clerkship that the level is more or less the same as in Denmark. I felt that I was well prepared.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In the clinical clerkship the style of teaching was very similar to UCHP. The doctors told us about the patients and the procedures and always asked if we had any questions. Futhermore we also sometimes had a 1 hour class where the teacher / doctor would cover a subject - this is also very similar to UCHP.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: My courses was my clinical clerkship where I visited 6 departments during my 12 weeks of stay. The departments were as following; neurosurgery, neurology, urology, cardiology, ENT and anesthesiology. I stayed at every department for 2 weeks.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If the student can choose I would recommend to visit the department of anesthesiology, ENT, urology and neurosurgery. My favorite department to visit was anesthesiology, since most the doctors spoke english, were very kind and the explained a lot and the also activated me a lot. The program was very structured, not too long days and I feel like I learned a lot.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to pay local insurance. This I was not told about. Luckily it was not a big amount - around 200-300 DKK, but I was a bit surprised.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was generally cheaper than I expected. It was quite affordable to get a lunchbox at the hospital, around 20 DKK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know, I was not informed about them. I know that the local students had some sports clubs they could attend, but since I was the only exchange student I am not sure that the university thought about offering me to join any kind of club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As described above I cannot really recommend any since I had no experience attending any non-academic activities at the university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: In general I would recommend the future exchange students to travel and visit different part of Japan - as much as possible in the weekends. Of course, Kyoto, Osaka, Tokyo. I personally really loved visiting Kanazawa and Ito. Ito is in Shizuoka and this prefecture is a really nice place and very accesbile from Isehara - I would really recommend some weekends in this prefecture for relaxing and just experiencing nice atmosphere.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took some time for me, but I think this because I was the only exchange student at this campus. There was no other student in my situation which was a bit difficult to deal with since the english abilities of the japanese students also is limited which I knew before beginning my program. But after sometime I adjusted more and found some japanese students who spoke more english and I could socialize with.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Have patience with them since a lot of them are shy but they really want to talk to you even though their english abilities might be a bit challenged. And if you feel like it just ask if you can have lunch together at the hospital - they are always up for it! Or even ask if you can hang out when you are finished at the hospital - maybe go out for dinner. Because they want to, they are just a bit shy to ask sometimes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't think there was any cultural difference I found particularly challenging. I wanted to hang more out with the local students but they studied a lot everyday when the program of the day finished, which I respected but it unfortunately made it difficult to hang out of the hospital sometimes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They showed a very sincere kindness and respect towards me. I really appreciated how I always felt that the local students wanted to help me and hang out with me. Even though their english abilities some times were challenged I particularly appreciated that they always tried to make contact to me anyway and talk to me. This made me feel very recognized!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Try to make some contact to the local students! 
2. Try to prepare yourself for the possibility that you might be the only exchange student at the campus 
3. You will 99% of the time only observe when you are at the hospital, not much of actual training (as in Denmark)
4. Explore a bit of the local area and prefectures nearby Kanagawa (not only the touristy places in Japan)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I actually I would have liked to know if there would be other exchange student from other countries - because I thought there would be, but I knew there was no other exchange student from Denmark besides me. I learned during my stay at Tokai University that in the autumn (which is when I was on exchange) the student from Denmark will be there alone. But in the spring there will be a total of 10 exchange students and one of the is from Denmark.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was to make true contact and friendships with some of the local students. I didn't expect this before attending. It made my experience so special and I am very grateful that I met so kind and thoughtful students who helped me to adjust to the hospital (and the rules) and get more comfortable during my stay. I am very grateful for the friendships I made with the local students and I could never have imagined that something like that would have happened.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: For me it was being on my own in a different country. Since there was no other exchange students I could not make plans to travel to other areas in Japan with others in my situation. I had a lot of time on my own - more that I expected, because I really expected that I would met other exchange students that I could have made plans with. But I really learned to do so much stuff alone during my stay which as been an absolutely amazing experience for me as a person.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
